methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center comparison of 48 vs 52 patients scanned with SMS+SS-EPI or RS-EPI, using transperineal 12+X biopsy as reference. Prior G*Power sample size calculation (d=0.8, alpha=0.05, power=0.90) is reported with minimum n=68. Two radiologists with 3 and 5 years of experience provide blinded scoring; inter-rater agreement (kappa >0.80; ICCs 0.77-0.88). Key weakness: the two groups were scanned with different sequences as standard of care on different days, not in the same patient, so inter-subject variability confounds image-quality comparisons. Also, the two sequences differ in FOV and matrix (206x206/128x128 vs 220x176/90x90), which is acknowledged but not controlled.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Comparing DWI acquisition techniques for prostate cancer has direct clinical relevance for MRI protocol selection. The demonstrated ADC-based AUC equivalence (0.925 vs 0.933, p=0.644) with approximately 2-minute time savings for SMS+SS-EPI is useful for scheduling and workflow. As a retrospective non-paired comparison with pathology gold standard, LoE maps to 4 (low-quality diagnostic cohort).

reporting_quality.justification: Appropriate reporting standard for a diagnostic accuracy study is STARD; not referenced. Key STARD items (participant flow diagram, sequence parameters, ROC analysis with AUC/sensitivity/specificity, reference standard described as 12+X transperineal biopsy) are present. Missing: explicit STARD checklist, blinding of index-test readers to biopsy results, timing between MRI and biopsy, handling of indeterminate results. Ethics approval number provided (2025[037]). No data or code availability; one imaging scanner manufacturer (Siemens Vida 3.0T) but sequence protocol details could be more complete.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim this is the first systematic comparison of SMS+SS-EPI vs RS-EPI in prostate DWI. Prior work in breast (Ohlmeyer 2019), rectum (Koeter 2022), cervix (Qian 2019), and bladder (Chen 2019, Takeuchi 2025) is cited. This is a sensible clinical extension to the prostate organ, but conceptually incremental. Finding of equivalent ADC-based AUC with time savings is pragmatically useful but not conceptually novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Writing is adequate but contains multiple typos and awkward phrasings ('SMS+SS EPI' mixed with 'SMS+SS-EPI', 'anatomical aberration', 'multipara metric', 'Soer jomataramI', 'Tan'Y'). Tables and figure numbers reference table-intensive comparisons. The objective metric comparison is internally clear but the subjective-vs-objective contrast (RS-EPI wins subjective, SMS wins SNR/CNR) is well explained. Some section-header punctuation issues ('Clinical dates' for Clinical data).

key_strengths: Pre-specified sample size calculation (G*Power, d=0.8, power 0.9, minimum n=68) with achieved n=100 meeting threshold
Two-reader blinded subjective and objective evaluation with high agreement (kappa >0.80; ICCs 0.77-0.88)
Clinically relevant finding: ADC-based AUCs equivalent (0.925 vs 0.933, p=0.644) with approximately 2-minute acquisition time savings for SMS+SS-EPI
Transparent reporting of sequence parameters (TR/TE, FOV, matrix, b-values, acceleration factor) enabling reproducibility
Appropriate use of transperineal 12+X biopsy with Gleason reporting as reference standard
key_concerns: Between-subject comparison: patients scanned with only one of the two sequences, introducing patient-level confounding that within-subject (paired) scans would eliminate
FOV and matrix differ substantially between sequences (206x206/128x128 vs 220x176/90x90) which confounds spatial-resolution interpretation of the subjective differences
No STARD checklist referenced; blinding timing between MRI reading and biopsy result unclear
Single-center single-vendor (Siemens Vida 3.0T) limits external generalizability
Writing contains numerous typos and inconsistent hyphenation in sequence names
No data or code/raw-image availability statement
chief_reviewer.rationale: Pragmatic clinical MRI sequence comparison with sensible sample size and appropriate reference standard, weakened by unpaired design and parameter asymmetries; suitable for Tier 3 imaging-oriented journal with minor revisions.
